newsitem.title: CHINA: Fancy mooncakes miss the mark in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Fancy mooncakes miss the mark in Shanghai.

text.p: Shanghai's makers of mooncakes, the sticky, sweet cakes Chinese eat at Mid-Autumn Festival, might have bitten off more than they can chew as tough competition has forced them into a price war, Business News said on Friday.
Shanghai bakers would produce 3,548 tonnes of mooncakes, worth about 150 million yuan ($18 million) for the festival, which this year falls on September 16, the newspaper said.

Despite price increases for ingredients, most of the city's 220 mooncake makers would charge the same as last year, it said, as the growing number of laid-off workers had eaten into Shanghai residents' disposable income.
Shanghai has about one million workers who have been laid-off from their jobs, and receive a portion of their salary from the state-owned enterprises that employed them, official media have said.

Some bakeries, most of them joint ventures, had missed the mark by trying to produce fancy mooncakes that did not conform to the traditional round shape or heavy sweet filling such as red bean paste and coconut paste, it said.
The new-fangled cakes often cost twice as much as the traditional style and had failed to win consumers, it said.
Some had been forced to cut their prices by half, it said, without further details.
